explanatory_strength.rationale: The claim is now stated in the only form that fits a non-operated mineral owner. The partition is producing wells at the producing decline (178,544 MMcfe, 7.27-year life, d=13.75%) plus the 8,783-location undeveloped inventory valued separately, with no volume in both. It fixes the category error running through the prior contract: proved reserves are 98% PD / 2% PUD by construction, because SEC rules bar a non-operator from booking PUDs it cannot commit to develop, so proved reserves were never the economic endowment. The 8,353 unbooked locations sit outside the reserve report but were audited and approved by CG&A, the same engineer.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Raised from 2. The fact I said was missing and unresolvable from the packet is now in it: location counts by basin, gross and net, audited. Volumes are basin-weighted rather than uniform, which matters because Mid-Continent is 50% of net locations on 9,314 ft laterals against Appalachia's 13,246 ft, so a uniform rate overstates the book by roughly 40%. Two independent estimates converge: 385-574 Bcfe basin-weighted against 543 Bcfe from the reserve report's own 65 MMcfe per booked location. Short of 5 because the EUR per 1,000 ft band is my assumption, not CG&A's, and no forward price deck exists anywhere in the packet.

downside_control.rationale: Raised from 2. The mandatory hedging covenant changes the risk shape: the Note Purchase Agreement requires fixed-price swaps on at least 75% of PDP volumes for 36 months from closing and 50% rolling thereafter, so this is not the unhedged commodity pass-through the deep dive describes. Leverage is about 1.0x against a 3.50x covenant, and the asset is fee-owned minerals that never expire. Held at 3 because no distribution is declared, conversion pace is entirely at operators' discretion, and depletion still equals CAFD.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Raised from 1 but still poor. Crediting the inventory moves base value from $5.72 to $8.76 and the high case to $12.81, improving the annualised return from -19.53% to -14.47% base and -9.70% high. It is negative in every case at $26.16. Paying roughly 2.7x PV-10 for an asset whose upside is contractually sold forward three years at a time is not a scarce-asset entry point.

votes.strongest_counter_explanation: The realisation haircut of 0.10-0.25 may be far too deep. It is a timing proxy standing in for a schedule nobody has built, applied to volumes 1.9-2.8x the entire proved book, so it is now the largest single determinant of value in the contract, ahead of the reserve report. If operators drill the Appalachian inventory at anything like the 126-198 wells/yr implied by WhiteHawk's 18% participation in new basin wells, the average location arrives sooner than a 35-58 year programme suggests and the correct haircut is nearer the 0.40-0.70 band the prior contract applied to booked non-producing volumes. At 0.40 the inventory component alone is worth roughly $9 per share and the total clears $14.
votes.most_important_missing_fact: Operator development schedules against WhiteHawk's specific acreage: permits, rig allocation and announced 2027 capital budgets for EQT, Antero, Range and CNX. That would convert the realisation haircut from a judgment into a dated conversion schedule.
falsifiers: An operator activity census showing conversion materially above 200 wells/yr, which would make the 0.10-0.25 haircut indefensibly deep.
The FY2026 reserve report carrying fewer than 6,000 gross undeveloped locations.
PV-10 per Mcfe moving outside $1.00-$2.00 on the next SEC deck.
specialist_findings: The scarce-asset lens's required evidence is now largely satisfied: legal economic claim, non-overlapping physical inventory, unit economics and remaining owner capital are established. Realisation timing remains a haircut rather than a schedule.
PV-10 and the producing component's base required return are both 10%, so the two legs stay discount-rate comparable.
The mandatory hedge is double-edged and the contract prices neither edge: it floors the downside the low case models and caps the upside the market is paying for.

Crediting inventory raised base value 53% without changing a single fact about the producing wells. That sensitivity is itself the finding: the answer is dominated by an assumption, not by the reserve report.

explanatory_strength.rationale: The bridge from reserve asset to Class A share is complete and every step sourced. My prior objection stands and is now quantified: no component charges recurring corporate overhead against asset value. Pro forma FY2025 G&A was $27.439m; capitalising even $8m per year over the 8.4-year proved life at 10% removes about $44m, roughly $1.57 per Class A share at the 82.1% interest.

votes.strongest_counter_explanation: PV-10 is an accounting floor, not intrinsic value: a trailing-twelve-month deck, a fixed 10% discount rate regardless of asset quality, and proved reserves only. Appalachian mineral packages transact above PV-10 for exactly those reasons, and WhiteHawk's operators are the best-capitalised in the basin. If 2.5x-3.0x PV-10 is where this asset class actually clears, my multiple measures the conservatism of a convention rather than an overvaluation. The packet still cannot test this, and after two rounds and a restored filing that is now a statement about the workspace rather than the company: we hold no comparable-transaction evidence for any mineral package.
votes.most_important_missing_fact: Arms-length transaction comparables for Marcellus and Haynesville mineral and royalty packages, expressed as a multiple of PV-10 and as dollars per net royalty acre. Established across two committee rounds as absent from the workspace entirely, not merely from this filing.
falsifiers: Comparable transactions showing Appalachian mineral packages clearing consistently above 2.5x PV-10.
A declared dividend above roughly $1.30 annualised per Class A share sustained through a full reserve-report cycle.
The FY2026 reserve report raising PV-10 above $500m.
specialist_findings: The conclusion survives the most generous available choices: pre-tax PV-10 rather than the after-tax standardized measure of $266.326m, the widest inventory band, and the shallowest haircut, and still no case returns capital at $26.16.
The earnout is treated conservatively: low and base assume the 1,250,000 units issue and dilute to 82.1%; only the high case keeps 86.0%.
The single largest input by value is now the realisation haircut, a judgment with a 0.05-0.40 allowed range rather than a filed number. Value moves roughly $5 per share across that band.
Uncharged corporate overhead makes this valuation too generous by about $1.57 per share, which strengthens rather than weakens the rejection.

explanatory_strength.rationale: Raised from 3. Seniority is respected, claims are not double-counted, and the capital structure is now fully specified rather than merely referenced. What the contract still does not do is move the commodity price across its cases, though the mandatory hedge materially reduces how much that omission matters over a three-year horizon.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Raised from 2, for a specific reason: the fact I named as most important and missing is now in the packet. The Note Purchase Agreement requires Consolidated Total Net Leverage of not more than 3.50x from the quarter ending 2026-06-30, an Asset Coverage Ratio of at least 1.00x, and a Liquidity Percentage of at least 10%. The Revolving Credit Facility carries a 3.00x test, and restricted payments including dividends require pro forma leverage below 2.00x. Against roughly $58-64m net debt and $64.405m pro forma Adjusted EBITDA that is about 0.9-1.0x, inside every test including the dividend gate. Short of 5 because nothing has survived a reporting cycle and the actual swap strikes are unfiled.

downside_control.rationale: Raised from 2 to 4, the largest move I have made, on three facts I did not previously have. Leverage headroom to 3.50x at about 1.0x actual. A mandatory hedging covenant putting 50-75% of PDP volumes on fixed-price swaps rolling 36 months. And 49 consecutive monthly dividends totalling roughly $37m paid pre-IPO, so the distribution is a continuation rather than an untested intention. A royalty funds no drilling capital, bears no lease operating expense and carries no plugging liability. This is a defensively financed entity and I priced it as though it were not.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Unchanged, and now explicitly the whole of my objection. Better credit terms improve the odds of surviving to collect a bad return; they do not make the return good. -14.47% base with no positive case anywhere. The cycle framing still cuts against the position: roughly 2.7x PV-10 is being paid on a $3.387/MMBtu deck already 59% above the $2.13 deck of the prior reserve report, so the multiple sits on top of a recovered price rather than a depressed one.

If the cyclical risk belongs in the 9-12% discount rate the contract already applies, then my rejection double-counts it and the correct credit-cycle vote on this packet is watch, not reject.

Without strikes I cannot tell whether the hedge floors CAFD near the modelled run-rate or well below it.
falsifiers: A filed swap schedule showing strikes at or above the $3.03 per Mcf realised price assumed here, which would firm the low case materially.

An acquisition track record replacing reserves accretively through a full gas cycle rather than the twelve-month PHX and TRR window.
specialist_findings: Contract cases still hold the SEC deck fixed, but the mandatory hedge makes that omission far less severe over three years than I judged in round one.

Applying the packet's own price elasticity, $2.13 deck to $0.827 per Mcfe of PV-10 and $3.387 to $1.422, a return to the prior deck takes PV-10 toward roughly $170m. The hedge blunts the cash-flow effect for three years; it does not blunt the asset-value effect.

The pro forma preferred dividend deduction of $7.076m equals the historical FY2025 figure exactly and appears unadjusted for the Series D redemption completed with IPO proceeds, making pro forma CAFD conservative on that line by roughly $4-5m.

The earnout is struck on Adjusted EBITDA the company itself defines and reports, on a measure carrying $21.8m of fee add-backs, four months after a restatement in management-fee recording. That governance exposure is unchanged by anything in the restored filing.

pre_mortem.failure_story: Capital is committed near $26 on an inventory story that is real but slower than assumed. The 8,783 gross undeveloped locations exist and CG&A audited them, but conversion is entirely at third-party operators' discretion and they allocate rigs to their own best rock, not to WhiteHawk's royalty position. At the disclosed 126-198 wells/yr participation the inventory is a 35-58 year programme; if gas softens and Appalachian operators cut activity by a third, the pace that holds volumes flat disappears and the producing book reverts toward its 7.27-year PDP life. Meanwhile the mandatory hedging covenant, which protected the downside, also caps the recovery: the Note Purchase Agreement requires fixed-price swaps on 50-75% of PDP volumes rolling 36 months, so the gas-price upside the market is paying roughly +1.7% to +4.6% perpetual growth for is contractually sold forward for three years at a time. Holders discover the position is structurally a fixed-income instrument on a wasting asset with an equity multiple attached. Depletion, which already equals CAFD ($36.451m against $36.317m pro forma), keeps net income negative; the board, gated at 2.00x leverage for restricted payments, sets an initial dividend well below the CAFD headline; and the equity re-rates from roughly 2.7x PV-10 toward asset value.
earliest_warnings: The first 10-Q reports net production below the 64,270 Mcfe/d Q1 2026 run-rate without an offsetting acquisition, confirming conversion is not keeping pace with the 13.75% PDP decline.
Operator capital budgets for 2027 showing Appalachian and Haynesville activity down materially, since WhiteHawk's 18% new-well participation is derivative of their spending, not its own.
An initial declared dividend materially below the ~$1.30 per Class A share the pro forma CAFD run-rate implies, or a stated policy of retaining CAFD for acquisitions.
Realised prices lagging spot as the mandated swaps roll on at lower strikes than the prevailing strip.
The FY2026 reserve report carrying materially fewer than 8,783 gross undeveloped locations, or negative revisions to the 206,473 MMcfe proved book.
Any repeat internal-control finding, given the April 22, 2026 conclusion that FY2025 statements could not be relied upon.
forensic_checks: Reconcile CAFD to net cash provided by operating activities every period. Pro forma FY2025 operating cash flow was $9.533m against $36.317m of CAFD, and pro forma Q1 2026 operating cash flow was NEGATIVE $10.714m against $9.959m of CAFD. Establish which add-backs are genuinely non-recurring rather than recharacterised operating cost.

Test the $21.795m management-fee add-back. It is $6.2m Base plus $3.7m Dividend Incentive plus $13.6m Liquidity Incentive less $1.7m internal compensation. The Liquidity Incentive Fee is IPO-triggered and never recurs, so the durable saving from the Internalization is roughly $8.2m, not $21.8m -- against a $130.0m purchase price.

Read the actual swap schedule once filed: notional volumes, strikes and tenor. The covenant sets a floor of 50-75% of PDP but not the price, and the pro forma $16.052m derivative gain says the existing book is materially in the money at the old deck.
Compare depletion to CAFD every period. While DD&A approximates CAFD the distribution is return of capital and the payout ratio on economic earnings exceeds 100%.

Independently sample the 8,353 unbooked locations against operator permits and rig schedules. CG&A audited their existence, not the timing of their development, and timing is what the 0.10-0.25 realisation haircut is guessing at.
Trace the Up-C ownership arithmetic: the prospectus states IPO purchasers hold 24.8% of OpCo indirectly, while 33.5% of the Company times 86.0% is 28.8%. Those do not tie.

short_source_coverage.detail: The frozen adversarial pass records no Tier-1 forensic short and no local short_reports/, and the third-party cross-check still indexes zero sources. Two months after IPO that is expected, but it means no independent adversarial party has examined this name and the absence of a short thesis carries no information.

unresolved_items: No 10-Q or 10-K has been filed since the 2026-06-10 IPO, so every operating figure remains pro forma and the swap book's actual strikes and tenor are unknown.
No dividend has been declared as a public company, though 49 consecutive monthly dividends totalling ~$37m were paid pre-IPO on the predecessor share classes.

The gas price deck is frozen at the SEC trailing $3.387/MMBtu in every case; no forward strip is in the packet, and for an entity whose revenue is near-linear in price with no cost offset that is the largest unpriced variable.
Operator drilling schedules, which determine the conversion pace the entire inventory component depends on, are third-party data absent from the filing.
No comparable-transaction evidence exists for Appalachian mineral packages, so the market's ~2.7x PV-10 multiple cannot be judged normal or rich.
Remediation status of the identified material weaknesses is not established.

explanatory_strength.rationale: Raised from 3. Seniority is respected, claims are not double-counted, and the capital structure is now fully specified rather than merely referenced. evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Raised from 2, for a specific reason: the fact I named as most important and missing is now in the packet. The Note Purchase Agreement requires Consolidated Total Net Leverage of not more than 3.50x from the quarter ending 2026-06-30, an Asset Coverage Ratio of at least 1.00x, and a Liquidity Percentage of at least 10%. The Revolving Credit Facility carries a 3.00x test, and restricted payments including dividends require pro forma leverage below 2.00x. Against roughly $58-64m net debt and $64.405m pro forma Adjusted EBITDA that is about 0.9-1.0x, inside every test including the dividend gate. Short of 5 because nothing has survived a reporting cycle and the actual swap strikes are unfiled.

downside_control.rationale: Raised from 2 to 4, the largest move I have made, on three facts I did not previously have. Leverage headroom to 3.50x at about 1.0x actual. A mandatory hedging covenant putting 50-75% of PDP volumes on fixed-price swaps rolling 36 months. And 49 consecutive monthly dividends totalling roughly $37m paid pre-IPO, so the distribution is a continuation rather than an untested intention. A royalty funds no drilling capital, bears no lease operating expense and carries no plugging liability. This is a defensively financed entity and I priced it as though it were not.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Unchanged, and now explicitly the whole of my objection. adversarial_review.strongest_failure_path: Capital is committed near $26 on an inventory story that is real but slower than assumed. The 8,783 gross undeveloped locations exist and CG&A audited them, but conversion is entirely at third-party operators' discretion and they allocate rigs to their own best rock, not to WhiteHawk's royalty position. At the disclosed 126-198 wells/yr participation the inventory is a 35-58 year programme; if gas softens and Appalachian operators cut activity by a third, the pace that holds volumes flat disappears and the producing book reverts toward its 7.27-year PDP life. Meanwhile the mandatory hedging covenant, which protected the downside, also caps the recovery: the Note Purchase Agreement requires fixed-price swaps on 50-75% of PDP volumes rolling 36 months, so the gas-price upside the market is paying roughly +1.7% to +4.6% perpetual growth for is contractually sold forward for three years at a time. Holders discover the position is structurally a fixed-income instrument on a wasting asset with an equity multiple attached. Depletion, which already equals CAFD ($36.451m against $36.317m pro forma), keeps net income negative; the board, gated at 2.00x leverage for restricted payments, sets an initial dividend well below the CAFD headline; and the equity re-rates from roughly 2.7x PV-10 toward asset value.

chair_synthesis.why_primary_method_dominates: WhiteHawk's claim is a royalty on a physical inventory held in fee through an Up-C, and only a paired owner-cash and unit-NAV method values both the cash the producing wells pay today and the inventory behind them without counting the same molecules twice. The pairing is now correctly populated for the first time. Corroborating methods remain subordinate for stated reasons: comparable transactions cannot lead because the workspace indexes zero third-party sources, and replacement cost is inapplicable to a mineral interest. The decisive structural fact, established this round, is that SEC rules bar a non-operated mineral owner from booking PUDs it cannot commit to develop, so WhiteHawk's proved reserves are 98% PD / 2% PUD by construction. Any method anchored on proved reserves alone values the company as if operators stop drilling forever. The two legs are summed over a partition of disjoint volumes, never averaged.
methods_rejected_for_averaging: The owner-cash and unit-NAV legs are additive over disjoint volumes: 178,544 MMcfe producing against an 8,783-location undeveloped inventory. They are not blended to manufacture a consensus number, and the contract reports no double-counting flags.

The 2026-08-10 range of $4.86/$5.72/$6.83 was not averaged with this one. It was superseded: it credited only the 430 booked locations and valued the other 8,353 audited locations at zero, which the restored filing shows to be wrong.
agreed_facts: Proved reserves at 2025-12-31 are 206,473 MMcfe (178,544 producing) with PV-10 of $293.690m and a standardized measure of $266.326m, per the CG&A reserve report.

There are 8,783 gross undeveloped locations and 28.0 net; 430 sit in the reserve report and the other 8,353 were audited and approved by CG&A. Basin-weighted these carry 385-574 Bcfe net, 1.9-2.8x the entire proved book.

The Note Purchase Agreement requires Consolidated Total Net Leverage of not more than 3.50x, Asset Coverage of at least 1.00x and Liquidity of at least 10%; the revolver adds a 3.00x test; restricted payments including dividends require pro forma leverage below 2.00x. Actual leverage is about 0.9-1.0x.

The same agreement mandates fixed-price swaps on at least 75% of projected PDP production for 36 months from closing and at least 50% rolling thereafter. Royalty revenue is therefore not an unhedged commodity pass-through.
49 consecutive monthly dividends totalling roughly $37m were paid pre-IPO on the predecessor share classes; no dividend has yet been declared as a public company.
Pro forma FY2025 CAFD is $36.317m against DD&A of $36.451m and a net loss of $32.330m; pro forma operating cash flow was $9.533m and pro forma Q1 2026 operating cash flow was negative $10.714m.
Contract value per Class A share is $6.12 / $8.76 / $12.81 against a price of $26.16, an annualised return of -18.74% / -14.47% / -9.70% over seven years.

recommendation.rationale: Two of three raters reject and the third votes watch; no rater approves and no rater finds a positive-return case in any scenario. The finding should be read narrowly: this rejects the security at $26.16, not the business, and the evidence base improved materially this round. Every rater raised at least two scores, and all three now record the packet as sufficient where two called it insufficient a day earlier. The remaining objection is uniform and simple: even crediting an audited inventory 1.9-2.8x the proved book, and even on the most generous case in the range, the contract cannot reach a positive return at this price. The committee does not size capital and does not decide; this routes to human_decision.json.

dissent_preserved.dissent: The 0.10-0.25 realisation haircut may be far too deep. It is applied to volumes 1.9-2.8x the proved book, making it the largest single determinant of value in the contract, ahead of the reserve report itself. If operators convert at anything like the 126-198 wells/yr implied by WhiteHawk's disclosed 18% participation in new Appalachian and Haynesville wells, the correct haircut is nearer 0.40 and the total clears $14. Crediting inventory raised base value 53% without changing one fact about the producing wells; that sensitivity is the finding.
dissent_preserved.chair_response: Accepted and elevated to the primary open item. The committee has moved the dominant uncertainty from 'does inventory exist' to 'when does it convert', which is progress, but the second question is not answered in this packet and the contract's range understates the uncertainty around it.

dissent_preserved.dissent: Raised downside_control from 2 to 4 on the covenant package, the mandatory hedge and the 49-month dividend record, and stated for a second round that its vote is on price rather than credit. dissent_preserved.chair_response: Recorded without override. A credit seat voting on price is a real structural comment on this committee's composition, not a defect in the vote, and the hedge-caps-upside point is the strongest argument yet advanced against the market's implied growth.

dissent_preserved.dissent: Holds that the packet suffices to determine asset value even though it cannot explain the market multiple, and that the omission of capitalised corporate overhead makes the valuation too generous by about $1.57 per share rather than too harsh.
